verdict.reasoning: The doctor (patient) states, "I'm kind of struggling to breathe at the moment" and the clinician opens with, "You've been having some difficulty breathing, is that correct?"
Patient says, "I got stung by a wasp recently... I've got a bit of a rash on my arm where I got stung" and later confirms the sting was "just a few minutes ago" and on the arm.
Patient reports, "I got stung by a wasp recently... I've got a bit of a rash on my arm where I got stung" and when asked when it occurred, says, "It was just a few minutes ago."

Patient: "potentially there's a bit of swelling in my lips and tongue. Feels a bit weird." Clinician: "your lips don't seem swollen to me right now" indicating subjective sensation without visible swelling.
Patient states, "I'm just kind of a bit anxious that it might get a bit worse. I just wanted to speak to someone."
Clinician asks, "Have you got a history of anaphylaxis?" Patient: "Not that I know of, no." Then, "Have you ever been given an EpiPen?" Patient: "I haven't, no."
Clinician: "Do you suffer from anxiety or panic attacks..." Patient: "Yeah, sometimes. Occasionally." Clinician: "Have you ever been on medication for that?" Patient: "No. No."
When asked about illnesses, patient says, "I've had eczema before. That's kind of the major thing."
Clinician: "Have you got a history of any allergies to anything?" Patient: "I'm allergic to penicillin."
Clinician asks about family history; patient replies, "Not that I think is particularly relevant, no, I don't have any," which describes it as non-contributory.
Clinician: "And you're living alone?" Patient: "Yes."
Clinician: "What do you work as?" Patient: "I am a computer scientist."

Patient: "Do you have any pets at home?" Patient: "I have a cat." Earlier: "And do you have allergies to any kind of cats or dogs or pets..." Patient: "Not that I know of. Yeah, I've been around dogs and cats."

Clinician: "Does it look red to you at the moment?" Patient: "It's slightly red... there's a bit of a... puncture mark." Clinician: "Is there any swelling... I couldn't see any." Patient: "It doesn't feel like particularly swollen." Warmth is not mentioned, so absence is acceptable as not documented.

Clinician states, "Your breathing seems all right to me right now" and later, "based on... how you're breathing... I don't feel that you're having a life threatening allergic reaction" and notes no stridor: "Thankfully you don't have anything like that right now" when describing stridor.
Clinician: "your, your lips don't seem swollen to me right now" and later focuses on swelling as a warning sign, implying none seen currently.

Clinician examines mouth/throat and then says, "based on how you look, how you're talking to me and how you're breathing... I don't feel that you're having a life threatening allergic reaction" and explains they were looking for swelling of "the tissues inside the mouth, the soft tissues of the airway" and does not find any, implying no soft tissue swelling observed.

Clinician concludes, "it seems to me that this is a localized allergic reaction. However, if anything changes..." and notes absence of key systemic signs: "Thankfully, I can't see any [lip swelling or breathing compromise] right now" and that they don't feel it's a life-threatening allergic reaction.

Patient describes feeling anxious; clinician responds, "You did the right thing and I can understand it is quite anxiety provoking" and later, "Sometimes a chat is all you need to calm things down," supporting mild anxiety related to the reaction.
Clinician: "you can get pyritone or chlorphenamine and you can take one tablet, four milligrams, up to about six times a day. Okay? Or you can just take a one a day."
Clinician educates: "So for example, you would have swelling of the lips, difficulty breathing, you might have something called stridor..." as signs to watch for.

Clinician: "if anything changes, if anything deteriorates, either make an appointment with us or go straight to ae... in some cases, if it's progressing rapidly, it's better to go straight to AE rather than to wait." Also notes urgent need if breathing deteriorates.

Clinician states, "on the basis of what you told me, I don't think you need any allergy testing. I think this is just a straightforward localized reaction..." and all treatment advised is over-the-counter antihistamines, implying no prescription medications needed at present.
Clinician: "If the redness in your arm spreads and it feels hot or, you know, you have signs of any localised infection, we may need to think about other treatments like an antibiotic."
Clinician: "I'm going to leave some information about anaphylactic reactions just for you to read about it."
Clinician advises, "Get back to us if you're feeling worried. Just have a low threshold for having a chat with us."
Same as plan-007: "Get back to us if you're feeling worried. Just have a low threshold for having a chat with us." and "Come back to us if you have any further issues."
